tagline.text: A U-shaped lane in Cubao where an old Marikina shoe mall became an indie culture hub

location.label: Location
location.text: 3 Gen. Romulo Avenue, Cubao, Quezon City

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (evenings are most comfortable in December–February)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600~2,000 (per person for food, drinks, a little shopping and transport, half-day basis)

children.text: Cubao Expo is a U-shaped, two-story shopping compound on Gen. Romulo Avenue in Cubao, Quezon City. It began in 1972 as a showcase for Marikina shoes and is now an indie culture strip of bars, cafes, vintage shops, galleries and craft studios. It is a good place to wander from afternoon into the night, with plenty to eat and browse.

Cubao Expo (often called Cubao X) is a multi-shop compound at 3 Gen. Romulo Avenue in the Cubao district of Quezon City, Metro Manila. The two-story buildings wrap around a central courtyard in a U shape, and they are packed with small restaurants, bars, cafes, thrift shops, galleries and craft studios. It feels nothing like a big mall; think of it as an alley where Manila's young artists and music lovers hang out.

Its history is interesting. According to local blogs and culture media, the compound began in 1972 as the Marikina Shoe Expo, a two-story arcade of shoe stores built to promote Marikina's shoe industry. As the shoe industry struggled, it was reportedly almost empty by the late 1990s, and in the early 2000s it reopened under its current name, Cubao Expo, with an arts and alternative-culture identity. A few traces of the shoe trade remain, for example in shops that make custom boots.

Today Cubao Expo is livelier in the afternoon and at night than during the day. Many bars and restaurants open around three or four in the afternoon and close between eleven at night and midnight, so the most common plan is to arrive near sunset, browse the shops, and move on to dinner and a drink. With used records, vintage items, streetwear, skateboards, collectible figures and pottery studios, it suits shoppers and anyone who wants photos with a distinctive atmosphere.

Be aware that the shops change often. Many shops mentioned in blogs from the early 2010s are gone, and some listed in 2023–2024 guides may already have changed. Treat the shop names, prices and hours in this guide as a reference, and check each shop's social media page before you go.

The layout of the 1970s shoe arcade is still intact, so you can walk a loop around the courtyard and browse the ground-floor and second-floor shops in turn. The shops are small, and peeking in from the doorway is often enough to get the feel. You can cover the whole compound in about
1 hour

blocks.title: Pottery and craft studios and local lifestyle shops

children.text: A pottery studio offers hands-on classes from about
and also sells finished ceramics. There are also shops selling eco-friendly products and stores for local designer streetwear, which makes the compound a good place to pick up souvenirs and gifts.

blocks.title: Bellini's Italian and other long-running restaurants

children.text: Bellini's, an Italian restaurant decorated with Italy-themed paintings and a ceiling mural, has been well known for many years. Pasta starts from about
. There is also a Hong Kong-style restaurant serving Asian dishes and a Japanese takoyaki stand.

Over the years the compound has hosted poetry readings, plays, skate street parties, book sales, music gigs and geek conventions. There is no fixed schedule, so look for events on the venues' social media around your visit.
Walk from the MRT/LRT Cubao station to Gen. Romulo Avenue. Take in the shape of the whole U-shaped compound from the entrance first so you know where things are.
Browse the used record and vintage shops. Check the condition of records yourself and ask whether the price is negotiable.
Rest with a coffee at a cafe, or go up to the second floor to look down over the whole compound and take photos.
Have dinner. You can choose between Filipino, Italian and Hong Kong-style restaurants, and popular places fill up, so go early.
Move on to craft beer or cocktails at a bar. It gets crowded and noisy at night, so keep your belongings in front of you.
Grab is the easiest way home. Public transport thins out late at night, so work out the timing in advance.
Many shops close on Mondays, so Tuesday to Sunday is the better time to go.

items.title: Full-day Cubao route
items.subtitle: From daytime shopping to the night scene

children.text: This route starts with a morning arrival. Most shops open between 10 and 11 AM, so going much earlier means closed doors.
Look around the pottery studio and local shops. Classes may need advance booking, so inquire through social media.
Have lunch at one of the restaurants in the compound. A light snack such as takoyaki also works.
Head to another sight in Cubao or rest in a nearby mall. This is the hottest part of the day.
Come back to Expo for dinner and beer.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) or a city hotel in Makati, BGC or Malate, Grab is the easiest option. Set your destination to Cubao Expo or 3 Gen. Romulo Avenue.
The distance is long and EDSA is very congested, so depending on traffic the trip can take
1 hour
or more. Avoid rush hour.
Taxi and Grab fares vary widely with time and demand, so no fixed amount is given.
Get off at Araneta Center-Cubao station on MRT-3 or Cubao station on LRT-2 and walk. One guide puts the walk from the MRT station at about
13 minutes
If you take the EDSA Carousel bus, a guide suggests getting off at the North Avenue stop and transferring to the MRT to cut down on walking. Check the latest announcements for routes and operation.

There is some street parking around the compound, but spaces are scarce at peak times and some user reviews say the surrounding area is not safe (no official guidance was found), so a paid lot is recommended.
One option is to park at Araneta City or the Gateway Mall lots and walk over. Check parking fees on site.

The compound is partly open-air, so rain and midday heat can be uncomfortable, but most shops and bars open in the afternoon, so the best time to go is after 4 PM. Once the sun drops, the heat eases and the shops come alive.
To avoid crowds, weekday evenings are best, while Friday and Saturday nights can be crowded and loud. In the rainy season bring an umbrella, and avoid Mondays, when some shops close.

Places to eat and drink are all clustered inside the compound, so you do not need to look for restaurants elsewhere. Close together you will find a modern take on Filipino food, an Italian restaurant, Japanese takoyaki, Chinese-style shops serving Cantonese dim sum and dry noodles, craft beer bars and cocktail bars. Plan on about ₱300~800 per person per meal. Opening hours differ from shop to shop, so if you want lunch, check which places are open first.

There is no lodging inside Cubao Expo, so stay at hotels around Araneta City and the Cubao area. If you plan to stay out late, a hotel near an MRT/LRT station is convenient, and many people also come by Grab from Makati or BGC. For specific hotels, choose using the latest reviews on booking sites.
Go after 4 PM. Many shops stay closed before noon, and some close on Mondays.
Carry both cash and a card. Some small shops accept only cash or e-payments.
Some secondhand shops have fixed-looking prices, but others accept bargaining, so ask politely.
Get to popular bars early to secure a seat. Seats fill up fast on Friday and Saturday nights.
Photography rules may differ from shop to shop; reviews mention them but no common policy was found, so ask staff before taking pictures.
Go around sunset and photograph the courtyard when the lights come on, for a great atmosphere.
Check current opening hours on Google Maps or each shop's social media page.
The Cubao area is crowded, so pay extra attention to your belongings and your ride home at night.
Pickpockets can operate in crowds, so keep your phone and wallet in front of you and your bag closed.
Parking is limited, and only user reviews, with no official guidance found, say parking on the surrounding streets is risky, so use a paid lot and do not leave valuables in the car.
Rather than wandering alone late, stay with your group and take Grab straight back to your hotel late at night.
Shops change often and hours are not fixed, so confirm that a place is open before making a long trip.
Bars are crowded and noisy in the evening, so daytime is better if you are traveling with children.
